market_holds: Spot is $0.2653 at the 2026-11-13 close (Yahoo daily bars). Market cap is about $37m on 140.3m shares (10-Q cover, 2026-08-07), against roughly $23m of debt. The stock is at its 52-week low, 67% below the 52-week high. It has fallen from about $0.44 before Q2, to $0.31-0.33 after Q2's -28.9% reaction, briefly to $0.38-0.41 on the BioHorizons dental deal (77.6m shares traded on 2026-08-28), then drifted steadily down to $0.27-0.28 through October and November, which spans the weak spine prints from Orthofix (2026-11-09) and Bioventus (2026-11-02). It is -9% over 5 and 20 sessions. There is no option chain. The usual move is a median 8.3% across 8 prints (baseline); the last four were -28.9, -4.0, +3.7 and 0.0. Guide: FY2026 revenue of $99-103m, cut from $101-105m on 2026-08-11. With H1 at $43.9m, that guide needs $55.1-59.1m in H2, or $27.5-29.5m a quarter, against a Q2 of $23.0m. One unconfirmed source, the Benzinga Korean page, gives sell-side consensus of $27.1m for Q3 and $30.1m for Q4. An older Seeking Alpha snapshot has FY at $96.2m, so the estimates are thin, one to three analysts, and probably stale from August. Price targets are $1.00-1.50, including Lucid's Buy initiation on 2026-09-02. Short interest is negligible at 0.3% of shares and 3.9 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30, per the sweep). Nantahala holds about 49%. Turnover is about $40k a day.
view: Q3 will turn on two things: whether revenue shows the H2 ramp the $99-103m guide needs (which usually means whether the guide is cut again), and liquidity. On revenue, the inputs point below the guide. Orthobiologics were $15.6m in Q1 2026 and $17.4m in Q2, and Q2 already held part of a quarter of HEMOBLAST, distributed since 2026-04-10. Even so, the 10-Q says orthobiologics fell year on year (Q2 2025: $19.4m), because the amnio line lost reimbursement. Spinal implant was about $5.5m a quarter. In 2025, orthobiologics dipped seasonally from Q2 to Q3 ($19.4m to $17.1m). Spine peers' Q3 prints since Xtant last spoke are soft: Orthofix cut its FY guide on U.S. spine weakness, and Bioventus bone graft substitutes fell about 6% on spine-procedure softness. My own build: underlying orthobiologics $15-16m, plus HEMOBLAST at $2.5-3m (management said 'over $1m a month gross as the transition completes'), plus a possible small BioHorizons stocking order, plus spinal implant at $5.3-5.7m. That gives about $23.5-26m for Q3, below the $27.1m figure and the $27.5m a quarter the low end of the guide needs. A second guide cut is more likely than not. On liquidity, cash was $9.9m at 2026-06-30, the revolver had $0.7m of availability, adjusted EBITDA ran at -$2.7m in Q2, the expanded sales force costs more, and MidCap had to waive the Q2 minimum-revenue covenant (Amendment No. 5, 2026-08-10). Cash at 9/30 is plausibly $5-7m. That makes another waiver, going-concern wording or a dilutive raise real risks in this release. Against all this, the market already prices distress: about 0.37x sales, down 40% since Q2 and sliding into the print, with peers' weak spine numbers already out. A merely 'less bad' quarter, a held guide or Nantahala-backed financing could lift a $0.27 stock 10-20% on very little volume. The balance tilts down, but not far enough, or with a clear enough gap to the price, to bet on.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the H2 gap. The sell-side numbers I could find ($27.1m Q3, $30.1m Q4) still sit on the guide, and my own arithmetic and the peers' spine softness put Q3 several million lower. The stock's steady slide to all-time lows, though, suggests holders already expect a cut. I cannot show that the gap is unpriced, only that the published estimates are stale.

recommendation.reason: My revenue build and the peer read-across make a Q3 shortfall and a second FY guide cut more likely than not, and liquidity is tight enough that financing or covenant news may come with the release. But at about 0.37x sales and at all-time lows after a 40% fall, the price already holds a distressed outcome, so the direction is short of 65%. Turnover of about $40k a day and $0.01 price steps (about 3.8% each) also make the realised move noisy.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 revenue of about $26m or more with the $99-103m guide held, or a Nantahala-backed financing or refinancing that removes the liquidity overhang, would make the reaction positive.

self_critique: The stock is priced for distress, and a revenue cut has been visible since August. Every bear point I have (the guide gap, peers' spine softness, tight cash) is public, and the 40% slide shows holders sold on it. In a thinly traded, majority-held $0.27 stock, a held guide, a HEMOBLAST ramp or a BioHorizons stocking order, or a financing that clears the liquidity question, could easily give +10-20% by 13:00. The consensus I lean on is single-source and may already sit below the guide (the $96.2m FY snapshot), in which case a cut would only meet expectations.
approach_notes: Rebuilding the line from the company's product-line tables (P3, own arithmetic) and the peer read-across (P6) did most of the work. P4's 'prove it is priced' cuts both ways here: I could not show the shortfall is unpriced, and a distressed price with stale estimates gave no clean gap.
